summary:
Noverra is an interactive website that I created to show how climate, geography, and agriculture are connected in different parts of the United States. It covers all 50 states and allows users to explore them using an interactive 3D globe.

On the website, users can choose a state and see different climate information, including temperature, precipitation, humidity, and solar radiation. I used NASA POWER data and geographic information from the U.S. Census Bureau. The project also includes agricultural information and references to USDA data.

I created Noverra because I wanted to make scientific information easier to understand and more interesting to explore. Climate conditions can affect agriculture, natural resources, and people’s everyday lives, but this information is not always easy to find in one place.

My goal was to bring these topics together in one platform where students and other users can explore, compare states, and learn more about the environment. I also wanted to show how NASA data can be used in a practical and educational way.
details:
I developed Noverra with the help of AI tools, mainly for coding, website development, and design. These tools helped me build the website structure, improve the code, create interactive features, solve technical problems, and develop the visual style. I also worked on the project idea, content, and organization of information.

NASA and Scientific Data Sources:

  • NASA POWER Daily API (daily climate and solar data)
  • NASA GIBS / Worldview (satellite imagery reference)
  • MODIS Terra (vegetation indices)
  • MODIS Aqua (additional vegetation information)
  • NASA SMAP L4 (soil moisture data)
  • NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (future climate projections)
  • U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb (official geographic boundaries)
  • PublicaMundi GeoJSON (backup geographic data)
  • USDA NASS Quick Stats (agricultural statistics)

Development Tools and Technologies:

  • JavaScript (interactive website features)
  • Lovable (website development and interface creation)
  • Claude (AI assistance with coding and technical solutions)
  • ChatGPT (coding assistance, planning, and content development)
  • AI-assisted design tools (visual design and creative ideas)
  • Netlify (website hosting and publication)

I also created a separate section on the website called “Grounded in Open Science”, where I listed the data sources and explained where the information comes from. I included links to the original providers and described which resources are already integrated, which are used as backup sources, and which are documented for possible future development. This helps users understand the origin of the information and makes the project more transparent and reliable.
